In the wide-band limit the dot self-energy is
\begin{equation}
\Sigma^r(\omega) = -\frac{i}{2}\Gamma, \qquad \Gamma \equiv \Gamma_L + \Gamma_R .
\label{eq:se}
\end{equation}
A B\"uttiker probe adds a dephasing rate, and the total width becomes
\begin{equation}
\Gamma = \Gamma_L + \Gamma_R + \Gamma_\varphi .
\label{eq:total}
\end{equation}
The branching ratios then sum to one,
\begin{equation}
\frac{\Gamma_L}{\Gamma} + \frac{\Gamma_R}{\Gamma} + \frac{\Gamma_\varphi}{\Gamma} = 1 .
\label{eq:branch}
\end{equation}
